report: The patient has lifelong stable alopecic patches; the affected right parietal-occipital patch is atrophic and boggy. Dermoscopy shows translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs, and head CT reveals no underlying osseous, vascular, neural, or soft-tissue defects. These findings are diagnostic of a congenital scalp defect, specifically aplasia cutis congenita. Recent tenderness is atypical but not infectious or neoplastic, as confirmed by dermoscopy and CT. Thus, aplasia cutis congenita of the scalp is the best explanation.
